messages.subject: Upcoming events of the Davis R Users' Group
messages.subject_clean: Upcoming events of the Davis R Users' Group
messages.body_plain:
Hello, D-RUGgies!

Our regular meetings continue in the DataLab classroom (room 360 Shields Library) on Wednesdays 10-noon. Here is a list of the events we have planned for those meetings this quarter - let us know if have an idea you'd like to see added to the for the fall or winter quarter!

Tomorrow we have Liza Wood to teach us about making an R package!
Next week we have a paper discussion - this quarter we will discuss a back-and-forth from The R Journal about R's software engineering culture, compared to a data analysis culture. The papers are short but sweet, so we hope you'll have a chance to read them in  advance of the group meetings. Links are below!

Current presentation schedule:
Sept 28: Brief intro to function writing and iteration (Liza)
Oct 5: Creating a package (Liza)
Oct 12: Paper discussion: Software Engineering and R Programming: A Call for Research <https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2021-108>
Oct 19: Making animated figures in R (Jesse)
Oct 26: Intro to web scraping (Liza)
Nov 2: Intro to text manipulation with regular expressions (Liza)
Nov 9: Paper discussion: We Need Trustworthy R Packages <https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2021-109>, The R Developer Community Does Have a Strong Software Engineering Culture <https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2021-110>, and The R Quest: from Users to Developers <https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2021-111>
Nov 16: Shiny Apps (Tara)
Nov 23: -- Thanksgiving week --
Nov 30:
Dec 7: --  Finals week --

-Wes

This is your weekly reminder of tomorrow's R Users Group work group. As usual, we'll be meeting from 10-noon on Wednesdays. For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

We are also seeking presenters! It is nice to mix things up with occasional presentations. In the past, we've had (15- to 45-minute) presentations ranging from data types, to tidyverse tools, to spatial data, to the Google Earth Engine plugin for R. If you would like to hone your teaching, need an excuse to perfect your cRaft, or want to show off a cool R trick you learned, shoot us an email and we can add your presentation to our calendar (see below)! Presentations can be in-person or virtual (and in-person presentations will be streamed for virtual attendees).

messages.subject: DataLab Affiliates call - deadline today.
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

we’re closing the 2022 solicitation for datalab affiliates today. The solicitation is here -

https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/2022/09/18/call-for-datalab-affiliates/

and I’d really like to encourage some D-RUG people to apply. This can be as simple as writing “I am involved in coordinating D-RUG on a regular basis”.

Here’s the form to fill out: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSe_ByJeHIvaXbF7W4Op5tMQquXsH4tZuGu9UduyKht3FOGAdg/viewform

The advantages to the D-RUG community would be:

* you’ll be looped into internal DataLab stuff like compute resource: we have a GPU node on farm to share, as well as an incoming CPU node and a bunch of disk space;
* note that RStudio Server is now up and running on farm! with conda! so you can run whatever version of R with whatever installed packages you want! see https://github.com/dib-lab/farm-notes/issues/44.
* we also plan to provide $$ in support of events, details TBD; think anything reimbursable (food, non-alcohol, etc.)
* DataLab affiliates get access to the DataLab space, too, if that’s something you’re interested in!

In exchange, you will be asked for a short blurb about what you are doing or did, and you’ll get semi-regular e-mails from me and other DataLab folk that you don’t even have to read. The only really strong request is for the blurb, because we need that to help justify our continued existence :). There will be no particular branding or affiliation statement expected.

And just to be clear, everyone is welcome to submit - please feel free to also think outside the box of current D-RUG activities, like “we’ll run an R hackathon” or “I want to run an R workshop” or something. But what D-RUG already does is awesome and we want to support it, and to do so within the scope of the affiliates program we just need one or two of the current coordinators/organizers to fill out the form above!

best,
—titus
(DataLab Faculty Director for, like, community and stuff)

I'm a psych PhD student, and I need to hire an R wiz that can easily edit complex functions, create a Rshiny platform, and has some knowledge of statistics (e.g., calculating kappa coefficient). The position is paid through the University (std 3, around 14.5 per hour), and it's completely remote.

messages.subject: Next week: writing tests and handling errors in your R functions. And, more paper discussions coming!
messages.subject_clean: Next week: writing tests and handling errors in your R functions. And, more paper discussions coming!
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies,
In a change of schedule, next week's meeting (10-12 Wednesday Oct. 26 in the DataLab classroom or via Zoom) will begin with a mini-workshop from ME, Wesley Brooks, talking about writing unit tests and handling errors in R functions.

During our paper discussion a week ago, everyone agreed that they are more of an "R User" than an "R Developer", and most of us had never written unit tests or error handlers. Well, I am here to help get us started on closing that gap. I'll go over the why and how of testing and error handling, and teach you all the basics of the testthat and rlang packages.

In a few weeks (Nov. 9) we will discuss the follow-up commentaries from the paper we discussed last week. There are four commentaries, each between 1-2 pages. So let's please read them all in the next few weeks and come on November 9 prepared to discuss how science interacts with R programming.

See you next week!
-Wes

> The Explorers Club is pleased to announce that our grant application portal is once again open to receive submissions.
>
>
>
>
> We are currently accepting applications for the following programs:
>  <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-r/>
> The Rising Explorer Grant
>
> The goal of this grant is to foster a new generation of explorers dedicated to advancing the scientific knowledge of our world.
>
> Average Award: $1,500.
>
> We recommend applying if: You are a high school student, college undergraduate, or independent researcher doing work at an equivalent level.
>  <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-y/>
> R <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-j/>olex Explorers Club Grant
>
> The Rolex Explorers Club Grants sends extraordinary young explorers into the field and promotes the significant role that exploration plays in addressing cutting-edge scientific questions, understanding our environment and the world we live in, and learning more about our history to protect our future.
>
> This program is open to all field science disciplines. In addition to demonstrating a spirit of exploration, candidates must put forward a project or research proposal that has a clear scientific rationale, represents original work, and has the potential for significant impact or new understanding.
>
> Historically, awards have been given in the amount of $10,000.
>
> We recommend applying if: You are a young explorer under the age of 35 conducting fieldwork to address a novel scientific, environmental, or historic question.
>  <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-t/>
> The Exploration Fund Grant <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-i/>
>
> This category supports exploration and field research for those who are just beginning their research careers.
>
> Awards are approximately $2,500 to $5,000.
>
> We recommend applying if: You are a graduate/post-graduate student or an early career scientist conducting fieldwork.
>
>  <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-d/>
> The Stephenson Explorers Advancement Program <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-h/>
>
> This category supports exploration and field research for marine exploration and conservation projects. The Philip Stephenson Foundation promotes marine exploration, protection, and conservation projects focused on adding value to people’s lives and the health of the environment.
>
> Awards will be $10,000.
>
> We recommend applying if:  You are a college undergraduate, graduate student, or an independent explorer conducting fieldwork focused specifically on marine research. (Open to those under 35.)
>  <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-k/>
> Fjällräven Field Grant <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-u/>
>
> The Explorers Club and Fjällräven share a common goal of understanding the world we live in by supporting and promoting a sustainable future through exploration and research. Furthermore, Fjällräven’s mission is to enable and inspire more people to spend time in nature by creating products that are of minimal impact to our environment and that will withstand a lifetime of use.
>
> Awards will be $5,000.
>
> We recommend applying if: You are an explorer enrolled in a University degree program doing scientific fieldwork in conservation, the environment or the natural sciences.
>  <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-p/>
> Exodus Exploration Without Boundaries Grant <https://theexplorersclub.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ntdjhlk-iuasukty-x/>
